Heavy shredders manufactured by heavy machinery brands crush the daily scrap tonnage delivered by transport drivers. Magnetic separators installed by recycling technology firms sort the ferrous metals, which are monitored by weight sensors calibrated by metallurgical technicians. Regulatory audits are performed by state inspectors based on these processing records. The script must report scrap yard locations, regional industrial parks, environmental agency regulations, shredder models, and heavy machinery brand names. The secondary query should list transport driver names, daily scrap tonnage, magnetic separator capacities, recycling technology firm names, metallurgical technician sensor readings, and state inspector regulatory audits for the month. Example input: august. Example output: scrap yard equipment and environmental sorting audits.

title: Orbital Space Debris Tracking
spec: Create a stored procedure `analyze(date)` that generates three reports about orbital debris. The database contains tables for radars, tracking sessions, detected objects, object classifications, satellite constellations, and collision warnings. The first query should return all detected objects that have an active collision warning with a satellite, showing the radar location, session timestamp, object classification name, and satellite owner. The second query must calculate the total mass of debris per radar location by combining radars, tracking sessions, objects, and object classifications. The third query needs to list all collision warnings escalated for evasion maneuvers, displaying the radar network region, tracking operator name, object telemetry, satellite designation, and the satellite constellation operator. For example, the first query might output a list of rows such as (Alaska North, 2023-10-12, Spent Booster, CommStar Corp). The second query would return rows like (Texas Array, 4500.5).

title: Intermodal Freight Railyard Scheduling
spec: Write a procedure `schedule(yard)` that outputs three daily schedules for a freight railyard. The tables include incoming trains, railcars, cargo containers, hazardous material classes, storage tracks, loading cranes, and truck outbound assignments. The first query must link incoming trains, railcars, cargo containers, and hazardous material classes to list the exact placement of all toxic cargo arriving today. The second query should match cargo containers on specific tracks to loading cranes and truck outbound assignments to generate a schedule of which crane lifts which container onto which truck. The third query combines tracks, railcars, cargo containers, truck assignments, and driver profiles to find all delayed containers, showing the original train arrival time, track location, crane operator name, and the assigned truck driver contact info. Example output for the second query is a list of rows like (Crane Seven, Container Alpha, Truck Nine). Example for the third query is (08:00 AM, Track Four, John Doe, 555-0199).

title: Historical Archive Digitization
spec: Create a procedure `audit(collection)` to generate progress reports for a digitization project. The system has tables for physical collections, archival boxes, paper documents, scanning workstations, imaging technicians, digital image files, and metadata tags. The first query must show the full lineage of every digital image file flagged for low resolution, linking the image file, scanning workstation, imaging technician, paper document, and archival box. The second query calculates the total scanned pages per collection by combining physical collections, boxes, documents, and image files. The third query retrieves all documents that possess restricted metadata tags, displaying the collection name, box shelf location, document condition, digital file format, and the specific tag description. For instance, the first query returns rows such as (File 102, Scanner B, Alice, Letter 5, Box 9). The second query yields (Presidential Letters, 1500).

title: Smart City Streetlight Maintenance
spec: Develop a script `maintain(district)` that prepares three lists for street maintenance crews. Data is stored in tables for city zones, neighborhoods, street light poles, led fixtures, sensor anomaly alerts, repair tickets, and technician dispatch crews. The first query must list all open repair tickets resulting from a sensor anomaly alert, showing the city zone name, neighborhood name, pole gps coordinates, led fixture model, and alert timestamp. The second query links technician dispatch crews, repair tickets, light poles, led fixtures, and replacement part inventory to show the required materials for today routes. The third query counts the number of resolved tickets per city zone by connecting zones, neighborhoods, poles, fixtures, tickets, and dispatch crews, filtering for fixtures installed in the last five years. An example output for the first query is (Downtown, Arts District, 40.71,-74.00, Lumina X, 2023-11-01). The third query returns (Uptown, 42).

title: Wholesale Seafood Market Auctions
spec: Write a stored procedure `settle(day)` that calculates auction payouts for a seafood market. The database tracks fishing vessels, landing docks, catch batches, species categories, auction lots, registered buyers, and final sale invoices. The first query links fishing vessels, landing docks, catch batches, and species categories to list the total weight of premium grade catches landed at each dock. The second query connects catch batches, auction lots, registered buyers, and final sale invoices to provide a receipt for each buyer showing vessel name, species name, lot weight, and final bid price. The third query identifies unpaid invoices by joining fishing vessels, vessel owners, catch batches, auction lots, invoices, and buyers, outputting the owner contact, vessel name, species description, and the outstanding balance. Example output for the second query is a list of rows like (Sea Hound, Bluefin Tuna, 200, 4500). Example for the third query is (Jane Smith, Wave Rider, Cod, 1200).

title: Mountain Rescue Helicopter Missions
spec: Implement a procedure `review(season)` that extracts three operational summaries for a mountain rescue service. The schema includes mountain ranges, base stations, rescue helicopters, flight crews, distress calls, mission logs, and medical outcomes. The first query should list every mission log where the medical outcome was critical, linking the mission log, distress call, mountain range, rescue helicopter, and flight crew to show the exact location, pilot name, and helicopter model. The second query counts the number of distress calls per base station by joining base stations, mountain ranges, distress calls, and mission logs. The third query retrieves all rescue helicopters that required maintenance after a mission, connecting helicopters, base stations, mission logs, distress calls, and caller demographics to analyze the circumstances of the harsh flights. For example, the first query outputs rows like (North Ridge, Sarah Connor, Alpine X2). The second query yields (Base Alpha, 15).

title: Heirloom Seed Bank Preservation
spec: Create a procedure `catalog(facility)` to report on seed preservation status. The tables contain botanical families, plant species, seed accessions, storage vaults, climate control sensors, germination tests, and research requests. The first query must link botanical families, plant species, seed accessions, storage vaults, and climate control sensors to find any seeds stored in vaults where the temperature exceeded the safe threshold. The second query connects plant species, seed accessions, germination tests, and laboratory technicians to list all accessions with a viability rate below fifty percent, showing the species common name, test date, and technician name. The third query joins seed accessions, plant species, research requests, requesting institutions, and shipping logs to display all pending deliveries, including the botanical family, vault location, and recipient address. An example output for the second query is (Blue Corn, 2023-05-12, Dr. Green). The third query returns rows like (Solanaceae, Vault B, 100 University Ave).

title: Tidal Power Generator Turbines
spec: Write a script `monitor(region)` that generates three diagnostics for a tidal energy farm. The database includes coastal bays, underwater arrays, turbine units, rotor blades, maintenance submersibles, engineering crews, and power output logs. The first query links coastal bays, underwater arrays, turbine units, rotor blades, and maintenance submersibles to identify any rotor blade with structural fatigue, showing the bay location, array depth, turbine model, and submersible inspection vehicle. The second query connects turbine units, underwater arrays, power output logs, and grid transmission nodes to calculate the average daily energy produced by each bay. The third query joins engineering crews, maintenance submersibles, turbine units, underwater arrays, and coastal bays to list all upcoming submersible dives, detailing the crew chief, submersible type, turbine status, and marine conditions. Example output for the first query is (Fundy North, 45, AquaStream 300, Sub One). The second query returns (Fundy South, 50000).

title: Industrial Diamond Cutting
spec: Develop a procedure `evaluate(month)` that tracks the workflow in a diamond cutting facility. The system stores rough stone parcels, individual diamonds, planned cuts, cutting machines, polishing technicians, quality certificates, and wholesale buyers. The first query links rough stone parcels, individual diamonds, planned cuts, cutting machines, and polishing technicians to show the complete history of every diamond that cracked during processing. The second query calculates the total carat yield per rough stone parcel by joining parcels, individual diamonds, planned cuts, and quality certificates. The third query connects individual diamonds, planned cuts, quality certificates, wholesale buyers, and shipping manifests to generate a dispatch list for flawless graded stones, including the parcel origin, final cut shape, certificate serial, and buyer destination. For example, the second query outputs rows such as (Parcel 99, 145.5). The third query yields (Botswana, Round Brilliant, Cert 8891, London).

title: Essential Oil Distillation Batches
spec: Implement a script `formulate(quarter)` to summarize essential oil production. The tables include partner farms, crop harvests, distillation runs, copper stills, essential oil batches, chemical lab tests, and fragrance product lines. The first query must link partner farms, crop harvests, distillation runs, copper stills, and essential oil batches to trace all batches produced from a specific farm, showing harvest date, still capacity, and final batch volume. The second query connects essential oil batches, chemical lab tests, lab technicians, and fragrance product lines to find any batch rejected for impurities, displaying the farm origin, distillation temperature, lab technician name, and the affected product line. The third query joins fragrance product lines, essential oil batches, distillation runs, crop harvests, partner farms, and agricultural regions to map out the geographic source of all premium grade fragrances. An example output for the first query is (2023-08-15, 500, 25.5). The second query returns (Valley Farm, 100, Alice, Floral Mist).

title: Competitive Trampoline Gymnastics
spec: Create a procedure `score(tournament)` that outputs the final standings and analyses for a trampoline event. The database contains gymnastics clubs, athletes, routine elements, element difficulties, execution scores, judging panels, and final rankings. The first query links gymnastics clubs, athletes, routine elements, element difficulties, and execution scores to calculate the total difficulty value attempted by each club. The second query connects athletes, routine elements, execution scores, judging panels, and final rankings to display every instance where a judge awarded a perfect execution score, detailing the athlete name, club affiliation, element description, and judge name. The third query joins final rankings, athletes, gymnastics clubs, routine elements, element difficulties, and execution scores to find all medalists whose routine included a triple somersault, showing their final score and club location. For example, the first query outputs (Sky High Club, 45.2). The second query yields (John Doe, Flip City, Double Pike, Jane Smith).

title: Vintage Car Auction Cataloging
spec: Write a script `publish(auction)` that compiles the catalog and logistics for a classic car auction. The schema includes consignor accounts, vintage vehicles, condition appraisals, auction lots, bidding paddles, final invoices, and transport carriers. The first query links consignor accounts, vintage vehicles, condition appraisals, auction lots, and bidding paddles to show the highest bid for vehicles in mint condition, including consignor name, vehicle make, appraiser notes, and bidder paddle number. The second query connects auction lots, final invoices, bidding paddles, registered buyers, and transport carriers to generate a delivery schedule for sold lots, listing the vehicle model, buyer address, invoice total, and carrier company. The third query joins consignor accounts, vintage vehicles, auction lots, final invoices, and condition appraisals to calculate the total sales revenue per consignor for vehicles manufactured before nineteen sixty. Example output for the second query is (Mustang, 123 Elm St, 55000, Safe Transport). The third query returns (Bob Roberts, 150000).

title: Organ Transplant Matching Network
spec: Develop a procedure `match(urgency)` that queries the database for potential transplant operations. The system tracks donor registries, recovered organs, tissue typings, hospital transplant centers, waitlist patients, surgical teams, and transport flights. The first query links donor registries, recovered organs, tissue typings, hospital transplant centers, and waitlist patients to find perfectly matching kidneys for highly urgent patients, showing donor blood type, organ condition, patient name, and hospital location. The second query connects waitlist patients, hospital transplant centers, surgical teams, and transport flights to list the required logistics for all scheduled surgeries today, including surgeon lead, flight number, and destination helipad. The third query joins recovered organs, donor registries, tissue typings, waitlist patients, hospital transplant centers, and surgical teams to report any cross matching conflicts, displaying the organ origin, mismatch reason, and the alternate patient on the list. An example for the first query is (O Positive, Excellent, Mary Jones, City Hospital). The second query yields (Dr. Smith, Flight 44, North Pad).

title: Commercial Hydroponic Lettuce Farming
spec: Implement a stored procedure `harvest(week)` that schedules greenhouse operations. The tables include greenhouse sectors, nutrient mixing vats, irrigation pumps, floating grow rafts, plant growth cycles, harvest logs, and grocery distributors. The first query links greenhouse sectors, nutrient mixing vats, irrigation pumps, floating grow rafts, and plant growth cycles to identify any rafts currently receiving suboptimal nutrient levels, showing the sector name, vat chemical balance, pump status, and planted crop variety. The second query connects floating grow rafts, plant growth cycles, harvest logs, grocery distributors, and delivery trucks to create a shipping manifest for mature lettuces, detailing the harvest weight, distributor name, and truck license plate. The third query joins greenhouse sectors, irrigation pumps, floating grow rafts, plant growth cycles, harvest logs, and nutrient mixing vats to calculate the total yield per sector for a specific month. For example, the second query outputs rows like (500, Fresh Foods, ABC 123). The third query returns (Sector Seven, 4500).

title: Wildlife Safari Tour Operations
spec: Create a procedure `guide(season)` that extracts operational data for a safari lodge. The schema contains wildlife reserves, territorial sectors, watering holes, animal sightings, tour vehicles, employed guides, and guest bookings. The first query links wildlife reserves, territorial sectors, watering holes, animal sightings, and employed guides to list all locations where endangered species were spotted this week, showing the sector name, watering hole capacity, animal species, and the guide who reported it. The second query connects guest bookings, tour vehicles, employed guides, animal sightings, and territorial sectors to print a personalized summary for each guest, detailing their vehicle type, guide name, and the list of animals they saw. The third query joins guest bookings, tour vehicles, employed guides, wildlife reserves, territorial sectors, and watering holes to find which vehicles require maintenance due to off road driving in muddy sectors. Example output for the first query is (North Sector, 5000, Black Rhino, Mark). The second query yields (Jeep, Mark, Lion).

title: Deep Sea Trench Bathymetry
spec: Write a script `map(expedition)` that analyzes data from an oceanographic survey. The database includes research vessels, autonomous submersibles, sonar arrays, dive tracks, mapped grid cells, thermal vents, and geological samples. The first query links research vessels, autonomous submersibles, sonar arrays, dive tracks, and mapped grid cells to show the complete path of any submersible that encountered extreme depth pressures, including vessel name, sonar frequency, and grid cell coordinates. The second query connects dive tracks, mapped grid cells, thermal vents, geological samples, and marine biologists to list all rock samples collected near active vents, detailing the vent temperature, sample mineral composition, and the biologist responsible. The third query joins research vessels, autonomous submersibles, dive tracks, mapped grid cells, thermal vents, and geological samples to calculate the total area mapped per research vessel in regions containing thermal vents. For example, the second query outputs (350, Basalt, Dr. Lee). The third query returns (Ocean Explorer, 1500).

title: Professional Bull Riding Events
spec: Develop a procedure `rank(season)` that aggregates statistics for a rodeo tour. The system stores tour arenas, stock contracting ranches, rodeo bulls, professional riders, event rides, judging scorecards, and sports medical reports. The first query links tour arenas, event rides, professional riders, rodeo bulls, and stock contracting ranches to list every ride where the rider stayed on for eight seconds, showing the arena city, rider name, bull name, and ranch owner. The second query connects event rides, judging scorecards, professional riders, rodeo bulls, and sports medical reports to identify any rides that resulted in a concussion, displaying the scorecard points, bull bucking style, rider age, and the attending medic notes. The third query joins stock contracting ranches, rodeo bulls, event rides, judging scorecards, professional riders, and tour arenas to calculate the average score of bulls provided by each ranch during championship finals. An example output for the first query is (Dallas, Tex Hunter, Tornado, Smith Ranch). The third query yields (Smith Ranch, 88.5).

title: Craft Chocolate Bean to Bar
spec: Implement a script `process(batch)` to trace the production of artisanal chocolate. The tables include cacao cooperatives, fermentation crates, shipping containers, roasting ovens, grinding melangeurs, chocolate batches, and retail wrappers. The first query links cacao cooperatives, fermentation crates, shipping containers, roasting ovens, and chocolate batches to trace the origin of a specific dark chocolate bar, showing the cooperative region, fermentation days, shipping port, and roasting temperature. The second query connects roasting ovens, grinding melangeurs, chocolate batches, retail wrappers, and quality tasters to list any batches that failed the flavor profile test, detailing the grinding time, wrapper design, taster notes, and the oven operator. The third query joins cacao cooperatives, fermentation crates, shipping containers, chocolate batches, grinding melangeurs, and retail wrappers to calculate the total bars produced from each cooperative, filtering for single origin organic certifications. For example, the first query outputs rows like (Ecuador, 5, Guayaquil, 120). The third query returns (Peru Co-op, 15000).

title: Artificial Pancreas Insulin Pumps
spec: A medical database stores information about patients, their implanted insulin pumps, daily calibration logs, continuous glucose monitor readings, automated bolus injections, manual meal entries, physician adjustments, firmware updates, and battery replacement events. Write a procedure `evaluate(patient)` that executes several queries to compile a safety report. The procedure must gather all glucose readings matched with bolus injections within a five minute window, link meal entries to subsequent glucose spikes, connect firmware updates to any pump error logs, and associate battery replacements with the assigned biomedical technician. Ensure that every patient profile connects to their primary physician, clinic location, and insurance provider. Provide the aggregated alerts and average response times. Example input: patient number 102. Output: 5 alerts, 3.2 minutes average response time.

title: Oceanic Plastic Cleanup Operations
spec: A maritime database tracks cleanup vessels, ocean current sensors, deployment zones, plastic collection nets, sorting facilities, daily collection manifests, recycling center shipments, vessel maintenance schedules, and crew assignments. Create a procedure `summarize(month)` that compiles a monthly yield report. The script must query vessels linked to their deployment zones and the current sensors in those areas. It needs to match collection manifests with the specific nets used and the sorting facilities that received the waste. Connect the sorted output to recycling shipments and their destination facilities. Finally, tie vessel maintenance events to the crew members involved and the shipyard locations. Output a summary of total tons recycled and vessel uptime. Example input: month of July. Output: 450 tons recycled, 94 percent vessel uptime.

title: Bionic Limb Prosthetics
spec: A clinical database records amputee patients, prosthetic limbs, neural sensor arrays, motor calibration sessions, joint wear logs, software patch histories, physical therapy appointments, therapist evaluations, and warranty claims. Implement a procedure `audit(region)` that generates a regional performance breakdown. Combine patient records with their prosthetics, neural sensors, and the specific clinic that fitted them. Link calibration sessions to joint wear logs and the software version active at the time. Match physical therapy appointments with therapist evaluations and connect any warranty claims to the specific component manufacturer and the approval officer. Return the average calibration score, the number of warranty replacements, and the therapy progression metrics. Example input: northern region. Output: average calibration score 88, 12 warranty replacements.

title: Nanomaterial Synthesizer Labs
spec: A laboratory system tracks synthesis reactors, chemical precursors, supply vendors, batch production runs, quality control scans, electron microscope images, purification centrifuges, technician shifts, and safety incident reports. Implement a procedure `report(reactor)` that outputs the full history of a specific machine. Combine the batch runs with the precursors used and the vendors that supplied them. Link quality control scans to the electron microscope images and the specific technician who authorized the batch. Connect the purification centrifuges used for each batch to their maintenance records and the safety incidents associated with that shift. Produce an overview showing the purity percentage of each batch, the associated vendor reliability, and the incident count. Example input: reactor serial 7. Output: 98 percent purity, 2 safety incidents.

title: Lunar Rover Navigation
spec: An aerospace database logs rovers, surface regions, traverse paths, obstacle avoidance events, solar panel efficiency readings, dust accumulation sensors, communication relays, earth station receivers, and mission control operators. Write a procedure `analyze(rover)` that calculates mission effectiveness. The logic must connect traverse paths to the surface regions and the specific obstacle avoidance events triggered. Link solar efficiency readings with dust sensors and the time of day. Match communication relays to earth station receivers and the mission control operator on duty during signal drops. Finally, tie the rover profile to its launch vehicle and manufacturing contractor. Output a chronological list of traverses with their power consumption and signal strength. Example input: rover designation 4. Output: list of 15 traverses with power usage and signal drops.

title: Exoplanet Transit Photometry
spec: An astronomical archive stores telescopes, digital imaging arrays, target star coordinates, observation sessions, light curve datasets, atmospheric interference logs, data processing algorithms, research grants, and lead astrophysicists. Write a function `compile(star)` that prepares an observation summary. The queries must link observation sessions to the telescopes, imaging arrays, and the target star. Connect light curve datasets to the data processing algorithms used and the atmospheric logs active during the session. Match the research grants to the lead astrophysicists and the institutions they belong to. Calculate the average dip in brightness, the confidence interval of the algorithm, and the primary funding source for the discovery. Example input: star designation 882. Output: 0.04 percent brightness dip, 95 percent confidence.

title: Magnetic Levitation Elevators
spec: A skyscraper management system tracks elevator cabins, vertical shafts, horizontal transit corridors, passenger call requests, magnetic rail segments, power substation feeds, emergency braking tests, maintenance technicians, and vendor warranties. Create a procedure `inspect(building)` that details transit efficiency and safety. Link the passenger calls to the elevator cabins and the horizontal corridors used. Match magnetic rail segments with the power substation feeds and the daily voltage fluctuations. Connect emergency braking tests to the maintenance technicians and the vendor warranties for the replaced parts. Output the average wait time per cabin, the total horizontal distance traveled, and the count of successful braking tests. Example input: building number 12. Output: 45 seconds average wait, 1200 meters horizontal travel.

title: Subterranean Hydroponic Farms
spec: An automated agriculture database contains growth chambers, led lighting arrays, nutrient solution reservoirs, plant crop varieties, daily harvest yields, water filtration units, atmospheric climate sensors, pest control interventions, and distribution trucks. Create a procedure `yield(crop)` that traces the production pipeline. Combine growth chambers with their lighting arrays, nutrient reservoirs, and the crop varieties planted. Link the daily harvest yields to the atmospheric climate sensors and the water filtration units active during the growth cycle. Connect pest control interventions to the specific chamber and the chemical supplier. Match distribution trucks with the harvest batches and the retail destinations. Return the total yield mass and the average nutrient consumption per chamber. Example input: lettuce crop. Output: 800 kilograms mass, 50 liters nutrient consumption.

title: Automated Warehouse Robotics
spec: A logistics system records mobile robots, charging stations, inventory racks, product categories, customer orders, packaging lines, barcode scanners, shipping carriers, and warehouse zones. Write a procedure `trace(order)` that reconstructs the fulfillment journey. The logic must link customer orders to the product categories and the inventory racks where they were stored. Match the mobile robots to their charging stations and the warehouse zones they patrol. Connect the packaging lines to the barcode scanners and the shift supervisors on duty. Tie the finalized order to the shipping carriers and the delivery destination regions. Output the time taken from rack retrieval to carrier handoff and the robot battery level at the time of retrieval. Example input: order number 993. Output: 14 minutes fulfillment time, 82 percent battery level.

title: Avalanche Prediction Sensors
spec: A mountain safety database logs seismic geophones, snowpack depth gauges, temperature probes, mountain peaks, ski resort boundaries, controlled detonation events, explosive inventory, safety patrol teams, and evacuation warnings. Write a procedure `assess(peak)` that models the avalanche risk history. Combine mountain peaks with the geophones, depth gauges, and temperature probes installed on them. Link controlled detonation events to the explosive inventory used and the safety patrol teams deployed. Connect evacuation warnings to the ski resort boundaries and the specific weather patterns recorded. Output a chronological log of detonations with the corresponding change in snowpack depth and the seismic response magnitude. Example input: summit number 3. Output: chronological log of 4 detonations and corresponding depth changes.

title: Deep Space Optical Communications
spec: A telemetry database tracks orbital lasers, ground telescope receivers, atmospheric distortion models, data packet transmissions, error correction algorithms, satellite orbits, launch vehicles, mission control stations, and shift commanders. Develop a function `audit(satellite)` that evaluates transmission integrity. The queries must link data packet transmissions to the orbital lasers, ground receivers, and the atmospheric distortion models active at the time. Match the error correction algorithms to the specific packet drops and the mission control station receiving the data. Connect the satellite orbits to the launch vehicles and the aerospace contractors. Return the packet loss percentage, the average distortion level, and the name of the shift commander during the highest loss period. Example input: satellite number 7. Output: 2 percent packet loss, moderate distortion level.

title: Brain Computer Interface Arrays
spec: A neuroscience database records implanted electrode arrays, neural decoding algorithms, motor cortex regions, patient profiles, thought translation sessions, robotic arm actions, calibration routines, surgeon logs, and ethical approval boards. Write a procedure `evaluate(patient)` that measures the interface accuracy. Combine patient profiles with the implanted arrays, motor cortex regions, and the surgeon logs from the implantation. Link thought translation sessions to the neural decoding algorithms and the specific robotic arm actions triggered. Connect calibration routines to the electrode arrays and the ethical approval boards overseeing the trial. Output the successful translation rate, the calibration duration, and the primary algorithm used. Example input: patient number 42. Output: 91 percent translation rate, 45 minutes calibration.

title: Swarm Robotics Search and Rescue
spec: An emergency response system tracks micro drones, deployment canisters, disaster zones, thermal imaging signatures, survivor acoustic pings, mobile command centers, field medics, medical supply payloads, and evacuation helicopters. Implement a function `reconstruct(disaster)` that details a rescue operation. Link the micro drones to their deployment canisters, mobile command centers, and the specific disaster zones. Match thermal imaging signatures to the survivor acoustic pings and the field medics dispatched to the location. Connect the medical supply payloads to the drones carrying them and the manufacturers of the supplies. Tie the final rescues to the evacuation helicopters and the receiving hospitals. Output the total survivors found and the average drone flight time. Example input: disaster zone 5. Output: 14 survivors found, 22 minutes average flight time.

title: Holographic Display Manufacturing
spec: A factory database contains laser emitters, optical diffraction gratings, glass substrates, assembly line robots, quality inspection cameras, cleanroom atmospheric sensors, packaging crates, freight transporters, and wholesale distributors. Write a procedure `trace(batch)` that audits the production quality. The logic must link laser emitters to the optical gratings, glass substrates, and the assembly line robots that combined them. Match quality inspection cameras to the cleanroom atmospheric sensors and the specific shift engineers. Connect the packaging crates to the freight transporters and the wholesale distributors receiving the goods. Return the defect rate per batch, the average cleanroom particle count, and the primary distributor for the batch. Example input: batch number 80. Output: 1 percent defect rate, 5 particles per million.

title: Atmospheric Carbon Aerosol Sampling
spec: A climate research system records stratospheric weather balloons, aerosol filter cartridges, mass spectrometers, flight trajectories, ground tracking radar, atmospheric pressure sensors, research laboratories, grant funding agencies, and lead climatologists. Write a procedure `compile(flight)` that generates a sampling report. Combine flight trajectories with the weather balloons, ground tracking radar, and the atmospheric pressure sensors. Link the aerosol filter cartridges to the mass spectrometers used for analysis and the research laboratories conducting the work. Connect the grant funding agencies to the lead climatologists and their academic institutions. Output the peak aerosol concentration, the altitude at which it occurred, and the duration of the flight. Example input: flight number 22. Output: 400 parts per million peak concentration, 25 kilometers altitude.

title: Symbiotic Algae Bioreactors
spec: A green energy database logs algae strains, cultivation tanks, light spectrum arrays, carbon dioxide injectors, lipid extraction centrifuges, daily biofuel yields, water recycling pumps, laboratory technicians, and energy grid buyers. Create a procedure `calculate(strain)` that analyzes biofuel production efficiency. Link cultivation tanks to the algae strains, light spectrum arrays, and the carbon dioxide injectors. Match daily biofuel yields to the lipid extraction centrifuges and the water recycling pumps active during the process. Connect the laboratory technicians to the specific tanks they maintain and the safety gear they wear. Tie the daily yields to the energy grid buyers and the distribution pipelines. Return the total liters of biofuel produced and the efficiency rating of the extraction. Example input: strain number 9. Output: 5000 liters biofuel, 85 percent extraction efficiency.

title: Kinetic Energy Recovery Systems
spec: An automotive database records flywheel modules, regenerative braking calipers, battery storage cells, test track laps, telemetry transmitters, vehicle prototypes, engineering teams, composite material suppliers, and crash test dummy sensors. Write a function `review(prototype)` that summarizes the energy recovery efficiency. Combine the vehicle prototypes with the flywheel modules, braking calipers, and the battery storage cells. Link test track laps to the telemetry transmitters and the crash test dummy sensors. Connect the engineering teams to the specific vehicle prototypes and the composite material suppliers for the chassis. Output the total joules of energy recovered, the maximum braking force, and the average battery temperature during the laps. Example input: prototype number 2. Output: 50000 joules recovered, 4 units peak braking force.

title: Autonomous Underwater Drones
spec: An oceanographic database logs submersible drones, sonar mapping arrays, deep sea trenches, battery pressure vessels, acoustic communication buoys, support ships, navigation waypoints, marine biologists, and specimen collection arms. Implement a procedure `map(trench)` that details the exploration dive. The script needs to link submersible drones to the sonar arrays, battery pressure vessels, and the specimen collection arms. Match navigation waypoints to the deep sea trenches and the acoustic communication buoys relaying the signals. Connect the support ships to the marine biologists on board and the home ports they deployed from. Return the total distance mapped, the number of specimens collected, and the lowest pressure vessel integrity reading. Example input: trench number 11. Output: 45 kilometers mapped, 8 specimens collected.

title: Exoskeleton Rehabilitation Therapy
spec: A physiotherapy database tracks exoskeleton suits, joint motor actuators, patient therapy plans, balance sensor pads, session progress metrics, clinical therapists, maintenance diagnostics, software firmware versions, and insurance authorization forms. Write a procedure `assess(patient)` that compiles a therapy progress report. Combine patient therapy plans with the exoskeleton suits, joint motor actuators, and the clinical therapists assigned. Link session progress metrics to the balance sensor pads and the software firmware versions active on the suit. Connect maintenance diagnostics to the specific actuators and the repair technicians. Tie the therapy plans to the insurance authorization forms and the billing codes. Output the total steps taken, the average balance score, and the number of maintenance faults. Example input: patient number 88. Output: 2000 steps taken, 92 percent balance score.

title: Microgravity Protein Crystallization
spec: A space station database logs protein solutions, crystallization chambers, microscope imaging modules, temperature control loops, downlink data streams, earthbound research teams, pharmaceutical sponsors, astronaut operators, and supply shuttles. Create a procedure `analyze(protein)` that audits the experiment results. The logic must link protein solutions to the crystallization chambers, microscope imaging modules, and the temperature control loops. Match downlink data streams to the earthbound research teams and the pharmaceutical sponsors funding the work. Connect astronaut operators to the specific experiments they initiated and the supply shuttles that delivered the solutions. Return the final crystal size, the temperature variance, and the primary research institution. Example input: protein number 5. Output: 2 millimeter crystal size, 0.1 degree temperature variance.

title: Synthetic Methane Production
spec: A fuel synthesis system records atmospheric scrubbers, hydrogen electrolyzers, methanation reactors, catalytic converter beds, gas storage tanks, distribution pipelines, safety pressure valves, control room operators, and industrial consumers. Write a procedure `audit(reactor)` that calculates the synthesis throughput. Combine methanation reactors with the atmospheric scrubbers, hydrogen electrolyzers, and the catalytic converter beds.
